title: Update on Whole-of-Government Response to COVID-19
what_it_is: Update on Whole-of-Government Response to COVID-19

sections.label: Update on evolving situation
sections.summary: The situation is evolving rapidly and a further update on the latest situation and strategy is provided.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The situation continues to evolve rapidly and we would like to take this opportunity to provide a further update on the latest situation and our strategy going forward.

sections.label: Singapore confirmed COVID-19 cases
sections.summary: Singapore has 558 confirmed cases, two deaths, 155 discharged, and most of the rest stable or improving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Currently, in Singapore, we have 558 confirmed cases, of which two have passed away; 155 have been discharged and most of the rest remain stable or are improving.

sections.label: Weekly case increase and imports
sections.summary: Cases more than doubled from 266 to 558 in a week, with almost 80% of new cases imported from countries other than China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In the past week alone, the number of cases in Singapore more than doubled, from 266 to 558 cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Almost 80% of these new cases were imported, all from countries other than China even though we continued to see around 1,000 residents and long-term pass holders return from China in the past week.

sections.label: COVID-19 tests per million
sections.summary: Singapore has done around 39,000 tests, about 6,800 per million, compared with South Korea and Taiwan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: To date, we have done around 39,000 tests for COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This translates to about 6,800 tests per million people in Singapore, compared with around 6,500 in South Korea and about 1,000 in Taiwan.

sections.label: Vaccine development and timeline
sections.summary: Duke-NUS is working with CEPI and partners on a vaccine trial, with WHO estimating earliest readiness next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In Singapore, Duke-NUS Medical School is working with Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations or CEPI, and international partners to develop a clinical trial for a vaccine, with plans to start testing sometime this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: With all these on-going efforts, WHO estimates that the earliest a vaccine will be ready would likely be sometime next year.

sections.label: NCID bed capacity
sections.summary: The 330-bed NCID was purpose-built with spare capacity and can be increased to over 500 beds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The 330-bed NCID was purpose-built with spare capacity and can be further increased to over 500 beds if need be.

sections.label: Community care facilities for COVID-19
sections.summary: MOH is setting up community care facilities and converting quarantine facilities for mild COVID-19 cases, with free treatment for residents and long-term pass holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We took this conservative approach earlier on in this epidemic, as there was little knowledge about the severity of the disease and we wanted to find out more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: However, we now know that about 80% of COVID-19 cases were mild to moderate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: They only require limited medical care and what we need really are isolation facilities to prevent them from infecting others, until they are free of the virus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, MOH is tapping on private capacity and setting up community care facilities, such as the collaboration with Concord International Hospital which started accepting well and stable COVID-19 patients last Friday and Mount Elizabeth Hospital which saw its first patient on Monday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are also converting some Government Quarantine Facilities, starting with D’Resort with a maximum capacity of about 500, for this purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As per public hospitals, Singaporean residents and long-term pass holders transferred to these facilities will continue to receive free-of-charge testing and treatment, except for those who have travelled overseas despite the travel advisory and contracted the infection while overseas.

sections.label: Discharge after negative tests
sections.summary: Patients are discharged back into the community only after full recovery and two negative tests over 24 hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Only when they have fully recovered and tested negative for the virus twice over a duration of 24 hours, will they be discharged back into the community.

sections.label: Expanded contact tracing capacity
sections.summary: Contact tracing capacity has grown from three to 20 teams, tracing up to 4,000 contacts daily, with the TraceTogether app launched.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In preparation for the expected surge in cases in the coming weeks, we have expanded our contact tracing capacity, from three teams when we started out, to 20 teams today, thanks to manpower support from colleagues from Public Service agencies, including the SAF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We can now trace up to 4,000 contacts each day and will continue to scale up our contact tracing capacity as needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: For example, last week, MOH and GovTech launched the TraceTogether app, which will capture data on whom you have come into contact with for some time.

sections.label: Responsible behaviour protects others
sections.summary: Studies show each ill person who behaves responsibly can protect two to three others from infection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Studies on COVID-19 have shown that for each ill person who behaves responsibly, we can protect two to three others from being infected.

sections.label: Guidelines to protect seniors
sections.summary: MOH introduced enhanced measures and guidelines encouraging seniors to maintain hygiene, stay home, and avoid group activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: MOH introduced an enhanced set of measures last week together with a set of guidelines to protect our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We encourage seniors to maintain good personal and environmental hygiene like everyone else and engage in more home-based activities rather than joining group activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Do not go out except for essential activities such as work or to buy food and supplies.

sections.label: Measures to slow virus transmission
sections.summary: The measures are extra brakes to slow transmission, prevent healthcare overwhelm, reduce cases, and protect seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The measures we have put in place are extra "brakes" to slow down the transmission of the virus, prevent our healthcare system from becoming overwhelmed, help bring the number of cases back down over time, and protect, particularly, our seniors.

sections.label: National unity against disruptions
sections.summary: The passage states that people must be prepared for disruptions and changes, and expresses confidence that a united whole-of-society effort can get the nation through together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We need to be prepared for disruptions to our daily lives and changes to how we do things.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But I am confident that if we stay united, with a whole-of-society effort, we can get through this together as a nation – SG United.

sections.label: Entry limits on visitors, work pass holders
sections.summary: It states that short-term visitors were disallowed from entering or transiting Singapore, and returning work pass holders were limited to those providing essential services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Earlier this week, we decided to disallow short-term visitors from entering or transiting in Singapore and to limit returning work pass holders to only those providing essential services like healthcare and transport.

sections.label: Singaporeans returning from UK, US
sections.summary: It states that about 1,200 Singaporeans are coming back every day from the UK and US alone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Just from UK and US alone, we are getting about 1,200 Singaporeans coming back every day.

sections.label: Stay-Home Notices for 38,000 residents
sections.summary: It states that residents on Stay-Home Notices must stay at their residence and avoid contact with others, even within the same household, and that there are now 38,000 such residents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They have to stay at their place of residence and avoid contact with others even within the same household.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We now have 38,000 residents on Stay-Home Notices.

sections.label: Returnees transported to designated hotels
sections.summary: It states that the regime was tightened, focusing on higher-risk returnees from the US and UK, who are transported from the airport directly to designated hotels for a 14-day self-isolation period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we have just tightened the regime with additional precautions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are focusing on returnees from the US and UK, given the higher risks, and we are now arranging for them to be transported from the airport directly to designated hotels to serve out the 14-day self-isolation period.

sections.label: Stay-Home Notices, quarantine, penalties
sections.summary: It states there are 38,000 Stay-Home Notices and 2,500 close contacts under quarantine, and that breaches can bring fines up to $10,000, jail up to six months, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The numbers give you a sense of proportion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are talking about 38,000 Stay-Home Notices because of the large volume of returnees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But within Singapore, the close contacts, we have 2,500 under quarantine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have put in place also very strict penalties for those who breach the requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They can be fined up to $10,000 or jailed for up to six months, or both.

sections.label: Tighter safe distancing measures
sections.summary: Another set of brakes, tighter safe distancing measures, aims to limit gatherings outside work and school to fewer than 10 persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our big worry is that these can become super-spreader events, spawning new clusters and potential runaway outbreaks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we have proceeded with another set of brakes yesterday – even tighter safe distancing measures with the aim of limiting gatherings outside of work and school to less than 10 persons.

sections.label: Suspending entertainment venues and gatherings
sections.summary: Entertainment venues are suspended, events and mass gatherings cancelled, and retail malls, museums and attractions must reduce density and prevent groups over 10, from Thursday 2359 hours until end of April.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But outside of schools and workplaces, we continue to see many gatherings of people and that is what we want to minimise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we are suspending all entertainment venues like bars, clubs and cinemas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Even though the numbers may be small, but children coming to these centres come from different schools and they intermingle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are cancelling and deferring all events and mass gatherings and we are putting restrictions on retail malls, museums and attractions where they have to reduce the density of people moving in these areas and ensure no coming together of groups of more than 10 persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These measures will take effect from Thursday, 2359 hours, and will be in place for at least a month until the end of April, that is, two incubation cycles.

sections.label: More drastic measures if needed
sections.summary: More drastic measures would include suspending schools and closing some workplaces, aside from those providing essential services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If so, we will need more drastic measures and that would include suspending of schools and closure of some workplaces, aside from those providing essential services.

sections.label: Enforcement and individual responsibility
sections.summary: The measures will be enforced, but ultimately compliance depends on individual responsibility and individual actions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: All of these measures we will try to enforce but ultimately it is about individual responsibility, individual actions to comply with these guidelines.

sections.label: Long fight and caretaker proposal
sections.summary: The fight will continue for many months, and the speaker asks the Government's constitutional position on a caretaker government proposal and election safety measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It almost seems like a life time ago, but in fact, we are only at the beginning of a very long fight.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This will continue for many more months till the end of the year and, perhaps, even beyond.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The coronavirus is, without a doubt, the biggest threat the world and Singapore has faced for decades.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, let us rally together and rise to this challenge because as SG United, we can beat the virus together and we will emerge stronger and toughened after this crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore's next General Election must be held by April 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, Dr Tan Cheng Bock has suggested that the President can exercise her soft power and form a caretaker government with some of the current Members of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In my view, having a caretaker government is not an answer to the long drawn crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, my question is: from the standpoint of the Constitution, what is the Government's position on such a caretaker proposal?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I have a second question: should the GE be held while COVID-19 is still in Singapore, what measures can be put in place to ensure the safety of Singaporeans during the election?

sections.label: Election deadline
sections.summary: An election must be held within three months, meaning on or before 14 April 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: An election must be held within three months of that, which means on or before 14 April 2021.

sections.label: Election deadline and COVID-19
sections.summary: An election must be held by 14 April 2021, though it is unknown when COVID-19 will stabilise.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We can hope and pray that things stabilise, but we do not know when the COVID-19 situation will stabilise – whether it will do so within the next year, by January, or by April 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: But what we do know is that an election must be held, must take place by 14 April 2021.

sections.label: AGC advice on delaying election
sections.summary: The AGC advises that delaying an election beyond the required date is unconstitutional unless a state of emergency is declared.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The advice of the AGC is that to delay an election beyond the required date in such a manner is unconstitutional.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The only circumstances when the election can be put off beyond the required date is when a state of emergency is declared.

sections.label: Election timing and disruption
sections.summary: Whether elections are held early or later, the next election will necessarily differ from past elections.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Even if the election takes place, it will not disrupt any of this.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Whether elections are held early or later, we will still have to work on the basis that the next election will necessarily be different from past elections.

sections.label: Measures, election timing, Stay-Home Notice
sections.summary: Measures affect all parties equally, no election timing decision is taken, and some returning Singaporeans breached Stay-Home Notices by going clubbing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Whatever measures taken will affect all political parties equally.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister said, no decision has been taken yet on the timing of the General Elections, but we have to plan on taking such additional measures to safeguard the health of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: And I stress that these precautions and measures will be needed whether the election is held early or later.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I think most Singaporeans are following the Government's advice very closely.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, there may be a small group of Singaporeans who disregard the Stay-Home Notice.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Instead of staying home, what we learn from some of the chat groups, is that those who returned went out clubbing.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, my question is, how do we deal with those who fail to comply with the Stay-Home Notice.

sections.label: Short-term visitor entry ban
sections.summary: On 22 March, all short-term visitors were barred from entering or transiting through Singapore as COVID-19 worsened worldwide.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But since then, of course, the COVID-19 situation across the world has grown considerably worse.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, on 22 March, we announced that all short-term visitors will not be allowed to enter into Singapore or transit through Singapore.

sections.label: Penalties for breaching SHN
sections.summary: First-time Stay-Home Notice offenders face up to six months' jail, a $10,000 fine, or both; repeat offenders face up to 12 months and $20,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If you breach the SHN, that could expose others to risk of infection, a first-time offender could face a jail term of up to six months, a fine of $10,000, of both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: For repeat offenders, they face a jail term of up to 12 months, a fine of $20,000, or both.

sections.label: Revoking passes of non-citizens
sections.summary: Passes of non-citizen residents and pass holders may be revoked, shortened or barred from re-entry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If you are not a Singapore Citizen, but you are a Permanent Resident, a long-term visit pass holder, a dependent pass holder, a student pass holder, where appropriate, we will not hesitate to revoke these passes, shorten their validity and also bar re-entry into Singapore.

sections.label: Silent infected traveller risk
sections.summary: A person who knew he was at significant risk of infection but stayed silent and flew knew others could be infected.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If he knew that there was a significant risk that he was infected but kept silent and went on the flight, then, he did so knowing that others could be infected.

sections.label: Electronic health declaration for travellers
sections.summary: ICA announced travellers must submit electronic health declarations from 27 March, shared with MOH to track high-risk country travel.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: They are in the frontline; we all have to support them and not expose them in this way.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, on 23 March, ICA has announced that travellers into Singapore will have to fill in electronic health declaration from 27 March onwards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: ICA will share this information – the electronic health declaration – with MOH so that they will know if a person has travelled to a high risk country.

sections.label: Reporting breached stay-home notices
sections.summary: The public should tell the Police if they know of stay-home notices being flouted or breached.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But there will always a few who are irresponsible in every society and they risk undoing our efforts and put other people's lives at risk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, if members of the public know of SHNs being flouted or breached, please tell the Police.

sections.label: Suspension of schools and workplaces
sections.summary: The next step, if necessary, would be suspending schools together with closing some workplaces except essential services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The next step, if it is necessary, would be, as I mentioned, suspension of schools, which has to also go together with closure of some workplaces, aside from those providing essential services.

sections.label: Triggering additional measures for cases
sections.summary: More imported cases that are contained may not need additional measures, but rising unlinked local cases may require activating the next brakes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: If we continue to see more cases coming in and a lot of them are imported cases, and we are able to contain and ringfence and isolate them, we may not need to trigger the additional measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But if we see more local transmitted cases, particularly unlinked ones, and that continues to rise, despite all that we are doing with strict safe distancing measures, then we may well need to activate the next set of brakes in order to slow down the spread of the virus.

sections.label: Suspension of religious gatherings
sections.summary: All religious congregations and services are suspended for the next month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For religious gatherings, we have made very clear there is a suspension of all religious congregations and services for the next month.

sections.label: Virtual meetings for SGX-listed companies
sections.summary: SGX-listed companies must hold virtual meetings, with smaller attendance due to no buffet and less tech-savvy shareholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With the latest measures, SGX-listed companies will have to hold virtual meetings; and the attendance at virtual meetings will be much smaller than the usual shareholders' meetings, first, because there is no more buffet and the second is that among the less tech-savvy, they may not be so comfortable participating in the virtual meetings.

sections.label: Home isolation for milder cases
sections.summary: Plans exist to let milder cases self-isolate at home with quarantine or stay-home notices, but community facilities suffice for now.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, it could be that they could still be carrying the virus at the end of the 14 days or they may even become symptomatic after the 14 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We do have plans if the situation warrants to allow the milder cases to self isolate at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We will serve them home quarantine or stay home notices to allow them to recover at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But at the moment we do not need to do that because we still have community facilities that we can tap on, but it is part of our options.

sections.label: Targeted testing for higher-risk exposure
sections.summary: Targeted testing may be done for those at higher risk of exposure, but blanket testing is not done because it creates false negatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: For those who have a higher risk of exposure, we may do targeted testing for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But we do not do blanket testing because that will first create a lot of false negatives, which give a false sense of assurance that "You are okay", and then, they go around spreading the virus.

sections.label: Guidelines for political parties
sections.summary: The task force will announce measures for all political parties to abide by regarding social distancing and other measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, to that end, can I confirm if the task force will be announcing some measures that all political parties can take into cognisance so that everybody is on the same page with regard to the task force's announcements vis-à-vis social distancing in other other measures?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is a rule or that is an advisory and a guideline that we put out to all organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And all political parties in this House, outside of this House will therefore have to abide by these guidelines and make adjustments to their activities.

sections.label: Housing support for frontline workers
sections.summary: There is a scheme to help frontline workers with housing support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: First, on the housing support for our frontline workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We do have a scheme to help frontline workers.

sections.label: Risk studies and surveillance
sections.summary: The risk is significantly lower, and studies on surveillance and serological tests are being carried out to find undetected underlying cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: It is not that there is no risk at all, but the risk is significantly lower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are carrying out studies on surveillance and as well as serological tests to determine whether there were underlying cases that were not detected.

sections.label: Keeping food outlets open
sections.summary: If stricter measures are imposed, F&B outlets and kitchens will remain open for take-out and volunteers can deliver items to vulnerable groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But if they do so, then the setting is such that it is safe, it is separated and the F&B outlets remain open, the kitchens remain open, because food manufacturers, kitchens still need to generate the food and some of that can be ordered for take-out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, these are things we are very mindful of and if indeed stricter measures are imposed, we will ensure some of these outlets remain open, in order for people to access food and essential supplies, and we can also mobilise volunteers who can help with the delivery of such items to vulnerable groups.

sections.label: CCTV spitting prosecution limits
sections.summary: CCTV footage caught the act but NEA cannot prosecute him because it is not spitting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The CCTV footage caught that but NEA cannot prosecute him because it is not spitting.

sections.label: Legal powers over public health
sections.summary: There are sufficient legal powers to go after behaviours that endanger public health and safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Even those behaviours that endanger the health and safety of the public, we have sufficient legal powers to go after them.

sections.label: Healthcare capacity tipping point
sections.summary: Minister Gan is asked to share the number of infected cases that would burden healthcare capacity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The second is: if Minister Gan can also share what is the number of infected cases or, in terms of its tipping point where our healthcare capacity will start to be under burdened, what is the number of infected cases that would actually get us to that tipping point?

sections.label: Patients sent to private hospitals
sections.summary: Patients have been sent to private hospitals, and those with mild and stable conditions to community isolation facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As I mentioned today, we have started to send patients to private hospitals and we are sending patients with mild and stable conditions to our community isolation facilities.

sections.label: Employers reducing public transport crowding
sections.summary: Companies and employers are urged to have staff work from home and use staggered hours to cut peak-period public transport volumes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In order to reduce crowdedness and in order to reduce volumes on public transport, particularly during the peak periods, it is vital that companies take action and employers take action to do two things: one, get as many of their employees and staff to work from home; and second, for those who really have to come to the office, put in place staggered hours.

sections.label: MOM and MTI engaging employers
sections.summary: MOM and MTI are engaging employers to step up telecommuting and reduce peak-hour loading on public transport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, MOM, Manpower Minister Josephine Teo, MTI, we are all reaching out engaging employers and getting them to step up and do more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have to go more aggressively on telecommuting in order to bring down the loading on the public transport system during peak hours.

sections.label: Stricter outbound travel rules
sections.summary: The Member asks whether outbound travel will be further restricted and how returning travellers will be managed and charged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My question is on outbound travel, Mr Speaker, and that is, I understand that we have been more and more stringent with outbound travel moving from advisory that says only for essential travel, and now moving to all travel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But my question is, in light of the fact that the situation is more heightened, will we be even stricter with the travel of our Singaporeans and Singapore residents overseas, knowing full well that if they travel out, a significant proportion of these outbound travellers will then have to come back?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, will the Government ever consider limiting travel, perhaps, requiring outbound travellers to seek unique and special permission, and then when they come back, how would we propose to manage these cases differently from those returning cases of people who have already been out for some time?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And the fact that when they are returning, upon returning they have to serve the full self-isolation period of 14 days and pay full cost for that as well.

sections.label: Police duties during contact tracing
sections.summary: Despite helping with contact tracing, the Police Force's duties are undiminished and criminals should not expect an easy time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Of course, there are also others, including the SAF who are helping us as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But I want to assure you that despite the involvement in the contact tracing, their duties as a Police Force has never been diminished.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And for criminals who think that they may have an easy time during this period, perish the thought.

sections.label: Congregation at bus stops
sections.summary: Congregation at bus stops and outside train stations means the sheer volume of commuters must be brought down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It would be in the bus stop, it will be outside the train station, there will still be a congregation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, I think before we talked about measures within a train, in the escalators, stations and all that, all necessary, we have to bring down the sheer volume.

sections.label: Daily messages in four languages
sections.summary: Over 900,000 messages are pushed out daily in English, Malay, Chinese and Tamil.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: For Members' information, today, we push out on a daily basis, something of the order of magnitude of over 900,000 messages each time and that is in the four languages – English, Malay, Chinese and Tamil.

sections.label: ICU capacity and manpower constraint
sections.summary: NCID ICU has capacity and room to expand, but manpower is the main constraint.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The capacity of ICU in NCID, we still have capacity and we have room to expand the capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But, I must say that the main constraint is not so much in the physical capacity, but on the manpower.

sections.label: Discharge from ICU to wards
sections.summary: Patients whose lung function has recovered are discharged to normal wards, though some stay over a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: If their lung function has recovered, we will discharge them to normal wards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But there are some who have been in there for quite some time, some may be more than a month.

sections.label: Closure duration based on exposure
sections.summary: Closure length depends on whether assessment finds no exposure or a broader range of people potentially impacted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: If the finding is that there is no exposure at all for that individual with other people around the infected person, then there may not be a need for an extensive closure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And then, you just closed for one or two days, make sure everything is disinfected, cleaned, and then, you can proceed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But, if the assessment is that there is a broader range of context within that particular environment and potentially more people may be impacted, then, they will give the advice to the centre that it is better to close for a longer period of time.

sections.label: Approvals for work pass holders re-entering
sections.summary: Work pass holders outside Singapore need approval to re-enter, with Citizens, Permanent Residents and Long-Term pass holders prioritised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Because, right now, we are requiring approvals before any one of the work pass holders can re-enter Singapore, if they are outside.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In order not to burden our healthcare system, we have prioritised Singapore Citizens as well as Permanent Residents and Long-Term pass holders coming back.
